nb16c8933c94.s: Command Area Development and Water Management is a component of which programme?
nb16c8933c94.x: Command Area Development and Water Management is a PMKSY component; IWMP was formed by merging DPAP, DDP and IWDP.

n067da73544c.s: Which of the following pairs (groundwater term – CGWB assessment category) is INCORRECTLY matched?
n067da73544c.x: CGWB categories include safe, semi-critical, critical, over-exploited and saline; 'perennial' is not one of them.

n131e697fd1f.s: Which continent ranks third in the world by area?
n131e697fd1f.x: The order is Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe and Australia.

nea39522fcd4.s:
Consider the following statements about deserts:
1. The Thar Desert extends through India and Pakistan.
2. The Great Victoria is the largest desert in Australia.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
nea39522fcd4.x: Both are true: the Thar spans India and Pakistan, and the Great Victoria is Australia's largest desert.

nworld-geography-12-19.s: Mount Cook is located in which mountain range?
nworld-geography-12-19.x: Mount Cook lies in the Southern Alps; Mont Blanc is in the Alps and Aconcagua in the Andes.

nb6f0e51b963.s: Which plateau is an intermontane plateau within the Andes?
nb6f0e51b963.x: The Bolivian Altiplano lies within the Andes; the Mongolian Plateau is in Central Asia and the Colorado is cut by the Grand Canyon.

n2ab5d3ad51c.s: Though Iran is not a party to UNCLOS, transit passage through the Strait of Hormuz binds it as:
n2ab5d3ad51c.x: The transit passage principle binds Iran as customary international law even though it is not party to UNCLOS.

n07f64c32ae3.s: The Dahlak Archipelago of the Red Sea lies off the coast of:
n07f64c32ae3.x: The Dahlak Archipelago lies off Eritrea on the western side of the Red Sea.

nworld-geography-8-19.s: The Niger river enters the Atlantic Ocean through the:
nworld-geography-8-19.x: The Niger enters the Atlantic through the Gulf of Guinea.

nworld-geography-7-3.s: The Huang He is called the 'Sorrow of China' mainly because:
o: Loess silt raises its bed, causing floods and course changes
It flows through a rift valley
nworld-geography-7-3.x: Heavy silt from the Loess Plateau raises the Huang He's bed, so it floods and shifts course.

nworld-geography-8-4.s: The Volga river drains into the:
nworld-geography-8-4.x: The Volga drains into the Caspian Sea; the Danube enters the Black Sea and the Thames the North Sea.

n90af75ccb5a.s: Normandy is a region of which country?
n90af75ccb5a.x: Normandy is in France; Sardinia belongs to Italy and Mallorca to Spain.

n8a169d85ee4.s: Which is the third largest island in the world?
n8a169d85ee4.x: By area the order is Greenland, New Guinea, Borneo and Madagascar.

n3811aa09410.s: Which of the following rivers is a feeder of Pulicat Lagoon?
n3811aa09410.x: Pulicat's feeders are the Arani, Kalangi and Swarnamukhi; the Pennar is not one of them.

new.s: The Club of Rome was founded in:
new.x: The Club of Rome was founded in April 1968 at the Accademia dei Lincei, Rome; its report 'Limits to Growth' came in 1972.

new.s: The part of a stock that can be used with present technology and is kept for future use is called a:
new.x: A reserve is the subset of stock usable with present technology; a stock is a resource for which technology is lacking.

new.s: Which of the following is an abiotic resource?
new.x: Abiotic resources are non-living, such as land, water and minerals; forests, micro-organisms and wildlife are biotic.

new.s: Depletion of groundwater is chiefly linked to:
new.x: Groundwater is depleted by deep bore tubewells for irrigation; brick production depletes topsoil.

new.s: India has about what share of the world's renewable water resources?
new.x: India has about 4% of the world's renewable water and 2.4% of world land for over 18% of the world's population.

new.s: The UNCCD defines desertification as land degradation in:
o: Arid, semi-arid and dry sub-humid areas
new.x: UNCCD (1994) defines desertification as land degradation in arid, semi-arid and dry sub-humid areas.

new.s: In land-use classification, cropland left unsown for up to one year is called:
new.x: Current fallow is land left uncultivated up to 1 year; other fallow is 1-5 years and culturable wasteland more than 5 years.

new.s: India's wastelands are mapped by the satellite-based National Wastelands Monitoring using:
new.x: National Wastelands Monitoring uses IRS remote-sensing data; IRS was commissioned in 1988.

new.s: In 2015 the IWMP was merged into PMKSY as its:
new.x: IWMP merged into PMKSY in 2015 and is now the Watershed Development Component (WDC-PMKSY).

new.s: The Watershed Development Fund was set up by:
new.x: The Watershed Development Fund was set up by NABARD; Neeranchal is the World Bank-assisted watershed project.

new.s: Under the National Forest Policy, 1988, what share of the country's total area was to be under forest?
new.x: NFP 1988 set 33% of the country under forest; the two-thirds target is only for hill areas.

new.s: India's first agroforestry policy, the National Agroforestry Policy, was adopted in:
new.x: The National Agroforestry Policy 2014 was India's first agroforestry policy.

new.s: The Centre's guidelines on Joint Forest Management were issued in:
new.x: MoEF issued JFM guidelines in 1990; Arabari (1972) was its forerunner and NFP 1988 introduced the idea.

new.s: The Appiko movement of 8 September 1983 began in which State?
new.x: Appiko began in the Salkani forest, Sirsi, Karnataka; Chipko was in the Himalayas.

new.s: Shorter fallow cycles in shifting cultivation in the north-eastern hills lead to:
o: Forest degradation and more soil erosion
new.x: Shorter jhum fallow cycles degrade forests and raise soil erosion.

new.s: Which country is the largest producer and exporter of softwood timber and wood pulp?
new.x: Canada is the largest producer and exporter of softwood timber and wood pulp.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about tank irrigation:
1. Andhra Pradesh ranks first in India's tank-irrigated area.
2. In Tamil Nadu, tanks are called Eris.
3. Tank irrigation is mainly linked with the Indo-Gangetic plains.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: AP ranks first (about 28-29%) and Tamil Nadu's tanks are Eris; tank irrigation is linked with Peninsular India, not the Indo-Gangetic plains.

new.s: India's annual water availability from rainfall is about:
new.x: India receives about 3,880 billion cubic metres of water a year from rainfall.

new.s: Andhra Pradesh's share of India's tank-irrigated area is about:
new.x: AP ranks first in tank irrigation with about 28-29% of India's tank-irrigated area; Tamil Nadu has over 23%.

new.s: The tanka, a traditional water-harvesting structure of Rajasthan, is a:
new.x: Tankas are rooftop cisterns; kuan are seepage wells, bawaris stepwells and johads crescent check dams.

new.s: Which traditional water-harvesting system is a seepage well of western Rajasthan?
new.x: Kuan or kui are seepage wells of western Rajasthan.

new.s: The Phad system of community canal irrigation is found in:
new.x: Phad is a community canal irrigation system of Maharashtra's Tapi basin.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (water-harvesting system – region) is correctly matched?
new.x: Katta is a temporary check dam of Dakshina Kannada, Karnataka; Kuhl is in Himachal/Jammu, Zing in Ladakh and Ahar-pyne in South Bihar.

new.s: The Parwan project, on a tributary of the Kali Sindh, is in which State?
new.x: The Parwan project is in Jhalawar, Rajasthan, on the Parwan, a Kali Sindh tributary.

new.s: The Ghataprabha (Hidkal) reservoir is in which State?
new.x: Ghataprabha (Hidkal) is in Karnataka, in the Krishna basin.

new.s: The Ukai dam is on which river?
new.x: The Ukai dam is on the Tapi in Gujarat.

new.s: The Hirakud dam on the Mahanadi lies about 15 km from:
new.x: Hirakud is in Odisha, 15 km from Sambalpur; its main dam is 4,801 m long.

new.s: The Ramganga (Kalagarh) dam in Uttarakhand mainly irrigates:
new.x: The Ramganga (Kalagarh) dam is in Uttarakhand and irrigates Uttar Pradesh.

new.s: The height of the Sardar Sarovar dam is:
new.x: Sardar Sarovar, on the Narmada near Navagam, Gujarat, is 163 m high.

new.s: The Rana Pratap Sagar power station at Rawatbhata was built with the help of:
new.x: Rana Pratap Sagar power station was built with Canada's help; the dam was begun in 1953 and opened in 1970.

new.s: The main canal of the Indira Gandhi Canal is about how long?
new.x: The Indira Gandhi Canal's main canal is 649 km long, from the Harike Barrage to western Rajasthan.

new.s: The Farakka Canal is located in which State?
new.x: The Farakka Canal is in Murshidabad, West Bengal, not Bihar.

new.s: How many river links did the National Perspective Plan (1980) identify?
new.x: The NPP (1980) has 30 links: 14 Himalayan and 16 Peninsular.

new.s: The flagship link of India's Interlinking of Rivers programme is:
new.x: Ken-Betwa is the flagship link of the interlinking programme implemented by NWDA.

new.s: Interlinking of Indian rivers was first proposed by:
new.x: M. Visvesvaraya first proposed interlinking, later K. L. Rao; Dastur proposed the Garland Canal.

new.s: The Upper Ganga Canal takes off from:
new.x: The Upper Ganga Canal takes off at Bhimgoda, Haridwar; the Lower Ganga Canal at Narora.

new.s: The Gang Canal, the oldest canal system of Rajasthan, was built in 1927 by:
new.x: The Gang Canal (1927) from Hussainiwala on the Sutlej was built by Maharaja Ganga Singh of Bikaner.

new.s: Jal Shakti Abhiyan, launched in 2019, is a:
o: Water-conservation campaign of the Ministry of Jal Shakti
new.x: Jal Shakti Abhiyan (2019) is the Ministry of Jal Shakti's water-conservation campaign.

new.s: The Rashtriya Barh Ayog (National Flood Commission) was set up in:
new.x: The Rashtriya Barh Ayog was set up in 1976; its report came in 1980.

new.s: The Rashtriya Barh Ayog put India's flood-prone area at about:
new.x: Its 1980 report put India's flood-prone area at about 40 million hectares.

new.s: The Hariyali scheme was launched on 27 January 2003 by:
new.x: Hariyali was launched by Atal Bihari Vajpayee for watershed and wasteland development through Panchayati Raj Institutions.

new.s: District Mineral Foundations are funded by:
o: The Consolidated Fund of the State
new.x: DMF, created by the 2015 MMDR amendment, is funded by miners' royalty-linked contributions, not the Consolidated Fund.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about amendments to the MMDR Act:
1. The 2015 amendment made auction of mineral concessions mandatory.
2. The 2023 amendment introduced the exploration licence.
3. The 2015 amendment funded the District Mineral Foundation from the Consolidated Fund.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: 2015 made auction mandatory and 2023 introduced the exploration licence; DMF is funded by miners' contributions, not the Consolidated Fund.

new.s: In Mineral Area Development Authority v. SAIL (2024), States can tax mineral-bearing land under which entry of the State List?
new.x: Mineral land falls under Entry 49 and mineral rights under Entry 50 of the State List; royalty is not a tax.

new.s: Mineral Area Development Authority v. SAIL (2024) was decided by a bench of how many judges?
new.x: A nine-judge bench held in 2024 that royalty is not a tax.

new.s: India's chromite is mined in the Sukinda Valley of:
new.x: Chromite comes from the Sukinda Valley, Odisha.

new.s: The International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea (ITLOS) is located in:
new.x: ITLOS is in Hamburg; the International Seabed Authority is headquartered in Jamaica.

new.s: Deep-sea polymetallic nodules are rich in:
new.x: Nodules carry manganese, cobalt, nickel and copper; sulphides carry copper, zinc, lead, iron, silver and gold.

new.s: The Mesabi Range iron-ore field of the USA lies in:
new.x: Mesabi is in Minnesota and Marquette in Michigan, both near Lake Superior.

new.s: The Ruhr region of Germany is famous for:
new.x: The Ruhr in Germany is a bituminous coal region; the Saar is also a coal region.

new.s: Kashagan in Kazakhstan is known as a(n):
o: Offshore oil field in the Caspian Sea
new.x: Kashagan is an offshore oil field of Kazakhstan in the Caspian Sea.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (region – resource) is correctly matched?
new.x: Pilbara in Western Australia is an iron-ore region; Minas Gerais is iron ore, Butte silver and Kimberley diamond.

new.s: Which country is the world's largest producer of manganese?
new.x: South Africa, with the Kalahari field, is the top manganese producer.

new.s: Which country was the world's largest producer of diamonds in 2025?
new.x: Russia produced about 30% of the world's diamonds in 2025; Botswana is a major producer.

new.s: Which country is the world's largest producer of lithium?
new.x: Australia (hard-rock) is the largest lithium producer; Bolivia has the largest identified resources.

new.s: The green colour of emerald is caused by:
new.x: Emerald (beryl) is green due to chromium or vanadium; sapphire is blue due to iron and titanium.

new.s: Emerald is a variety of which mineral?
new.x: Emerald is beryl, a beryllium aluminium silicate; ruby and sapphire are corundum.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about gemstones?
o: Ruby gets its red colour from chromium
Sapphire is blue because of iron and titanium
Ruby and sapphire are different minerals
Emerald is a variety of beryl
new.x: Ruby and sapphire are the same mineral, corundum (Al2O3); only the trace element differs.

new.s: Which region of India has fertile alluvium and rich groundwater but few minerals?
new.x: The Indo-Gangetic plains have fertile alluvium and rich groundwater but few minerals.

new.s: Evergreen forests and west-flowing rivers characterise which resource region?
new.x: The Western Ghats are marked by evergreen forests and west-flowing rivers.

new.s: Forests, hydropower and jhum lands characterise which resource region of India?
new.x: The Himalaya and NE hills are the region of forests, hydropower and jhum lands.

new.s: How many countries does Africa have?
new.x: Africa has 54 countries, the most of any continent; Asia has 48 and Europe 49.

new.s: The mean elevation of Antarctica is about:
new.x: Antarctica's ice sheet gives it the highest mean elevation, about 2,300 m; Asia's is 923 m and North America's 760 m.

new.s: Which continent has the highest percentage of land under plains?
new.x: Europe has the highest percentage of plains; Australia has the maximum per-capita land.

new.s: Which country is the second largest in the world by area?
new.x: The order is Russia, Canada, USA, China, Brazil, Australia, India; the USA is third.

new.s: The Canada-USA border, the world's longest international border, is about:
new.x: The Canada-USA border is 8,891 km; Russia-Kazakhstan is 6,846 km and Chile-Argentina 5,308 km.

new.s: The Galapagos Islands belong to:
new.x: The volcanic Galapagos Islands are part of Ecuador, not Peru.

new.s: The USA bought Alaska from the Russian Empire in:
new.x: Alaska was bought by the treaty of 30 March 1867.

new.s: The capital of Nigeria is:
new.x: Abuja is Nigeria's capital; Accra is Ghana's and Nairobi Kenya's.

new.s: Which continent has no landlocked country?
new.x: North America has no landlocked country; South America has Bolivia and Paraguay.

new.s: The second longest mountain range of the world is the:
new.x: After the Andes (~7,000 km) come the Rockies (~4,800 km), the Great Dividing Range (~3,500 km) and the Himalayas (~2,400 km).

new.s: The Sierra Nevada of California is an example of a:
new.x: Sierra Nevada is a block mountain; the Rockies, Alps and Himalaya are young fold.

new.s: The highest peak of the Rockies is:
new.x: Mount Elbert (4,401 m) is the highest peak of the Rockies.

new.s: The Caucasus Mountains lie between the:
new.x: The Caucasus, crossing Russia, Georgia, Azerbaijan and Armenia, lie between the Black Sea and the Caspian.

new.s: The highest peak of the Drakensberg is:
new.x: Thabana Ntlenyana (3,482 m, Lesotho) is the highest Drakensberg peak; Mafadi (3,450 m) is second.

new.s: The Andes are formed where the South American plate meets the:
new.x: The Andes rise where the oceanic Nazca plate and the South American plate meet.

new.s: The Great Dividing Range runs parallel to which coast?
new.x: The Great Dividing Range is in eastern Australia, parallel to the east coast, not in Africa.

new.s: The highest peak of North America is:
new.x: Denali (Mount McKinley) in Alaska, USA is North America's highest peak.

new.s: The highest peak of Europe is:
new.x: Elbrus (5,642 m, Caucasus, Russia) is Europe's highest; Mont Blanc is the highest of the Alps only.

new.s: The highest point of Kilimanjaro is:
new.x: Kilimanjaro's highest point is Uhuru on the Kibo cone; Mawenzi and Shira are its other cones.

new.s: In Reinhold Messner's Seven Summits list, the peak for Australia/Oceania is:
new.x: Messner's list has Puncak Jaya (Indonesia); Bass's list has Kosciuszko.

new.s: The height of Mount Kilimanjaro is about:
new.x: Kilimanjaro is 5,895 m; Elbrus 5,642 m, Aconcagua 6,961 m and Mont Blanc 4,807 m.

new.s: The Meseta plateau is located in:
new.x: The Meseta is the plateau of the Iberian Peninsula (Spain).

new.s: The Anatolian Plateau of Turkiye lies between the:
new.x: The Anatolian plateau lies between the Pontic and Taurus ranges.

new.s: The average elevation of the Tibetan Plateau is about:
new.x: The Tibetan Plateau, highest and largest, averages about 4,500 m.

new.s: The Columbia Plateau of north-west USA is a:
new.x: The Columbia plateau, like the Deccan, is a volcanic or lava plateau.

new.s: The area of the Indo-Gangetic Plain is about:
new.x: The Indo-Gangetic Plain covers about 6,52,000 sq km, over 2,400 km long.

new.s: The Great Basin of the USA lies between the:
o: Sierra Nevada and the Pacific coast
new.x: The Great Basin lies between the Rockies and the Sierra Nevada.

new.s: The Great Artesian Basin of Australia lies near the:
new.x: The Great Artesian Basin (~1.7 million sq km) lies near the Great Dividing Range.

new.s: The largest hot desert of the world is the:
new.x: The Sahara of North Africa is the largest hot desert.

new.s: The driest place on Earth is the:
new.x: The Atacama of northern Chile and southern Peru is the driest place on Earth.

new.s: A crescent-shaped sand dune is called a:
new.x: A barchan is a crescent-shaped dune; seifs are longitudinal, yardangs and zeugen are erosional forms.

new.s: The Pampas grasslands are found in:
new.x: The Pampas are temperate grasslands of Argentina and Uruguay.

new.s: The temperate grasslands of South Africa are called:
new.x: The Veld is South Africa's temperate grassland.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (grassland – region) is correctly matched?
new.x: The Steppes stretch across Eurasia from Ukraine to Mongolia; the Prairies are North American, the Pampas Argentinian and the Downs Australian.

new.s: The Levant refers to the:
new.x: The Levant is the eastern Mediterranean coast: Israel, Jordan, Lebanon and Syria.

new.s: The Nullarbor Plain is located in:
new.x: The Nullarbor is a limestone plain of southern Australia along the Great Australian Bight.

new.s: The lowest point of Australia lies in the:
new.x: The Lake Eyre basin of central Australia holds Australia's lowest point.

new.s: The Guiana Highlands are located in:
new.x: The Guiana Highlands span Venezuela, Guyana and Brazil in northern South America.

new.s: The busiest inland waterway of the world is the:
new.x: The Rhine, not the Danube, is the busiest inland waterway.

new.s: Which is the second longest river of Europe?
new.x: The Volga is Europe's longest river and the Danube second.

new.s: The Niger river rises in the:
new.x: The Niger rises in the Fouta Djallon and enters the Gulf of Guinea.

new.s: The Hoover Dam is on which river?
new.x: The Colorado, which cut the Grand Canyon, has the Hoover Dam.

new.s: The White Nile and Blue Nile meet at:
new.x: The White Nile (from Lake Victoria) and Blue Nile (from Lake Tana) meet at Khartoum.

new.s: The Mekong drains into the:
new.x: The Mekong flows from the Tibetan Plateau through Indo-China into the South China Sea.

new.s: The Amur river drains into the:
new.x: The Amur, on the Russia-China border, flows into the Sea of Okhotsk.

new.s: Europe's largest seaport, at the mouth of the Rhine, is:
new.x: Rotterdam lies at the Rhine mouth; Hamburg is on the Elbe.

new.s: The Volga rises in the:
new.x: The Volga rises in the Valdai Hills and enters the Caspian.

new.s: Lisbon is situated at the mouth of which river?
new.x: Lisbon lies at the mouth of the Tagus.

new.s: Kyiv is situated on which river?
new.x: Kyiv is on the Dnieper (APPSC Group 1, 2022).

new.s: New Orleans is situated on which river?
new.x: New Orleans is on the Mississippi, not the Missouri.

new.s: The largest alkaline lake of the world is:
new.x: Lake Van in Turkiye is the largest alkaline lake; Turkana is the largest desert lake.

new.s: Lake Urmia is located in:
new.x: Lake Urmia is in Iran.

new.s: Which is the largest lake of South America?
new.x: Maracaibo, a lagoon in north-west Venezuela, is the largest lake of South America.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Great Rift Valley lakes?
o: Lake Malawi lies at the southern end of the chain
Tanganyika lies in the western (Albertine) branch
Lake Victoria lies within the eastern rift branch
Lakes Albert, Edward and Kivu lie in the western branch
new.x: Lake Victoria lies between the two rift branches, not within either.

new.s: The only sea without land boundaries is the:
new.x: The Sargasso Sea in the North Atlantic, named after sargassum weed, has no land boundaries.

new.s: Which of the following countries borders the Baltic Sea?
new.x: Poland borders the Baltic; Norway does not.

new.s: The Bering Strait connects the Pacific Ocean with the:
new.x: The Bering Strait between Russia and the USA links the Pacific and the Arctic.

new.s: The Bass Strait separates Australia from:
new.x: The Bass Strait between Australia and Tasmania links the Tasman Sea and the Southern Ocean.

new.s: The Suez Canal was opened in:
new.x: The 193.30 km Suez Canal opened in 1869.

new.s: The largest river island of the world is:
new.x: Majuli on the Brahmaputra is the largest river island.

new.s: The largest island of Asia is:
new.x: Borneo is the largest island in Asia, shared by Indonesia, Malaysia and Brunei.

new.s: The second highest waterfall in the world is:
new.x: Tugela in South Africa's Drakensberg is the second highest after Angel Falls.

new.s: The Iguazu Falls lie on the border of:
new.x: Iguazu, the largest fall system, lies on the Argentina-Brazil border.

new.s: The Victoria Falls is known as:
new.x: The Victoria Falls on the Zambezi (Zambia-Zimbabwe) is called 'the Smoke that Thunders'.

new.s: The largest freshwater lake of India by volume is:
new.x: Wular (J&K) is the largest by volume; Kolleru (AP) is the largest by area.

new.s: Kolleru Lake lies between the deltas of:
new.x: Kolleru, a Ramsar site, lies between the Godavari and Krishna deltas.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about India's water institutions:
1. The Central Water Commission handles surface-water planning and flood control.
2. The Central Ground Water Board handles groundwater.
3. The National Water Development Agency implements Interlinking of Rivers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: All three are correct: CWC handles surface water and flood control, CGWB groundwater, and NWDA interlinking of rivers.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (region – resource) is NOT correctly matched?
new.x: Butte in the USA is known for silver; Katanga is copper, Witwatersrand gold and the Ruhr coal.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about river conservation schemes:
1. The National River Conservation Plan (1995) covers rivers other than the Ganga main stem.
2. Namami Gange was launched in 2014.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Both are correct: NRCP (1995) covers rivers other than the Ganga main stem, and Namami Gange began in 2014.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (mineral – world's top producer) is correctly matched?
new.x: Kazakhstan was the top uranium producer in 2023; the top producers of gold, copper and nickel are China, Chile and Indonesia.

new.s: Which of the following dam – river pairs is NOT correctly matched?
new.x: Ban Sagar is on the Son, not the Narmada; the Pamba Project is on the Pamba and Idukki on the Periyar.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about grasslands:
1. The Downs are temperate grasslands of eastern Australia.
2. The Llanos are tropical grasslands of Venezuela and Colombia.
3. The Savanna is a temperate grassland.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The Downs (eastern Australia) and Llanos (Venezuela, Colombia) are correctly placed; the Savanna is a tropical grassland.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a young (Alpine) fold mountain range?
new.x: The Appalachians are an old fold range of North America; the Alps, Andes and Atlas are young fold.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about deserts:
1. The Gobi extends into Russia and Kazakhstan.
2. The Kalahari lies in the Southern Hemisphere.
3. The Namib is one of the oldest deserts.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The Kalahari (Botswana, Namibia, South Africa) is in the Southern Hemisphere and the Namib is one of the oldest deserts; the Gobi lies only in Mongolia and China.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (range – location) is correctly matched?
new.x: The Atlas spans Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia; the Taurus is in southern Turkiye, Hindu Raj in northern Pakistan and the Drakensberg in South Africa and Lesotho.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (strait – water bodies connected) is wrongly matched?
o: Bab-el-Mandeb – Red Sea and Gulf of Aden
Dardanelles – Black Sea and Aegean Sea
Bosphorus – Black Sea and Sea of Marmara
new.x: The Dardanelles link the Sea of Marmara and the Aegean; the Bosphorus links the Black Sea and Marmara.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about lakes of the world:
1. The Caspian is the largest freshwater lake by area.
2. Tanganyika is the longest freshwater lake.
3. Titicaca is the highest navigable lake.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Tanganyika is the longest freshwater lake and Titicaca the highest navigable; the Caspian is saline, and Superior is the largest freshwater lake by area.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Great Lakes of North America?
o: The Detroit River links Huron and Erie
The Straits of Mackinac link Michigan and Huron
new.x: Lake Ontario is the smallest and easternmost Great Lake; Superior is the westernmost.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (island – country) is correctly matched?
